title: Chemical Element Names
description: Chemical element names according to the guidelines set by the Office of the Royal Society

sections.html:
Element names with definitions from the 1999 Royal Institute Dictionary

Chemical Element Names

Thai name

Definition

actiniumแอกทิเนียม (Actinium)Element number 89, symbol Ac. A metal; a silvery-white solid that melts at 1050 °C. A naturally occurring radioactive element.
aluminiumอะลูมิเนียม (Aluminium)Element number 13, symbol Al. A metal; a silvery-white solid that melts at 660 °C. It has many uses, e.g. alloyed with other metals and used to make kitchenware.
americiumอะเมริเซียม (Americium)Element number 95, symbol Am. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
antimonyพลวง (Antimony)Element number 51, symbol Sb. A metal; a brittle silvery-white solid that melts at 630.5 °C. It has the special property of expanding when it solidifies, and is used in alloys with other metals.
argonอาร์กอน (Argon)Element number 18, symbol Ar. An inert gas making up about 0.94 percent of air by volume. Used to fill light bulbs and fluorescent tubes.
arsenicสารหนู (Arsenic)Element number 33, symbol As. A solid with 3 allotropes: grey, black and yellow arsenic. A highly toxic element.
astatineแอสทาทีน (Astatine)Element number 85, symbol At. A non-metal; a solid. A naturally occurring radioactive element.
bariumแบเรียม (Barium)Element number 56, symbol Ba. A metal; a soft silvery solid that tarnishes quickly in air. Melts at 714 °C. Barium compounds are used in the paint, glass and fireworks industries.
berkeliumเบอร์คีเลียม (Berkelium)Element number 97, symbol Bk. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
berylliumเบริลเลียม (Beryllium)Element number 4, symbol Be. A metal; a white solid that melts at 1277 °C. Used in corrosion-resistant alloys with other metals.
bismuthบิสมัท (Bismuth)Element number 83, symbol Bi. A metal; a brittle reddish-white solid that melts at 271.3 °C. A poor conductor of heat and electricity, it has the special property of expanding when it solidifies, and is used in low-melting alloys with other metals.
bohriumโบห์เรียม (Bohrium)Element number 107, symbol Bh (not yet added to the Royal Institute Dictionary)
boronโบรอน (Boron)Element number 5, symbol B. A metal in the form of a fine brown powder or yellow crystals that melts at 2300 °C. Used in the steel and glass industries.
bromineโบรมีน (Bromine)Element number 35, symbol Br. A non-metal; a dark red liquid that evaporates easily, with a strong pungent odour; toxic and irritating to the nasal membranes. Boils at 58.8 °C. Bromine compounds are used in medicine and photography.
cadmiumแคดเมียม (Cadmium)Element number 48, symbol Cd. A metal; a soft silvery solid that melts at 321 °C. A good absorber of neutrons, it is made into rods called control rods in nuclear reactors.
caesium; cesiumซีเซียม (Caesium)Element number 55, symbol Cs. A silvery metal that is highly reactive chemically. Melts at 28.7 °C.
calciumแคลเซียม (Calcium)Element number 20, symbol Ca. A metal; a soft white solid that melts at 838 °C. An important component of bones, teeth, marble and limestone.
californiumแคลิฟอร์เนียม (Californium)Element number 98, symbol Cf. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
carbonคาร์บอน (Carbon)Element number 6, symbol C. A non-metal; a solid with several allotropes, such as diamond and graphite. Carbon is one of the most important elements in living things.
ceriumซีเรียม (Cerium)Element number 58, symbol Ce. A soft grey metal that melts at 804 °C.
chlorineคลอรีน (Chlorine)Element number 17, symbol Cl. A non-metal; a greenish-yellow toxic gas with a pungent, choking odour. Used to disinfect water, in the manufacture of hydrochloric acid and bleaching powder; many insecticides, such as DDT, contain chlorine as a key component.
chromiumโครเมียม (Chromium)Element number 24, symbol Cr. A hard silvery metal that melts at 1875 °C. Used in the manufacture of stainless steel, extra-strong steel for tools, and in chrome plating.
cobaltโคบอลต์ (Cobalt)Element number 27, symbol Co. A hard silvery metal that melts at 1495 °C. Alloyed with other metals to give them special properties; for example, with iron it makes it harder, and magnets made from it are exceptionally strong. Cobalt compounds are used to give a blue colour in the glass and ceramics industries.
copperทองแดง (Copper)Element number 29, symbol Cu. A metal; a soft red solid that melts at 1083 °C. It is easily beaten into thin sheets and drawn into wire, and is a good conductor of heat and electricity.
curiumคูเรียม (Curium)Element number 96, symbol Cm. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
dubniumดุบเนียม (Dubnium)Element number 105, symbol Db (not yet revised in the Royal Institute Dictionary)
dysprosiumดิสโพรเซียม (Dysprosium)Element number 66, symbol Dy. A metal; a solid that melts at 1407 °C.
einsteiniumไอน์สไตเนียม (Einsteinium)Element number 99, symbol Es. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
erbiumเออร์เบียม (Erbium)Element number 68, symbol Er. A metal; a soft, lustrous solid that melts at 1497 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
europiumยูโรเพียม (Europium)Element number 63, symbol Eu. A metal; a very soft grey solid that melts at 826 °C. Used to absorb neutrons to control nuclear reactions, and as a phosphor in colour television sets, etc.
fermiumเฟอร์เมียม (Fermium)Element number 100, symbol Fm. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
fluorineฟลูออรีน (Fluorine)Element number 9, symbol F. A non-metal; a greenish-yellow gas with properties similar to chlorine but more chemically reactive.
franciumแฟรนเซียม (Francium)Element number 87, symbol Fr. A metal; a solid that melts at 27 °C. A radioactive element.
gadoliniumแกโดลิเนียม (Gadolinium)Element number 64, symbol Gd. A very rare metal; a solid that melts at 1312 °C.
galliumแกลเลียม (Gallium)Element number 31, symbol Ga. A silvery-white metal; a solid that melts at 29.78 °C and boils at 2100 °C. Used in high-temperature thermometers; the compound gallium arsenide is used as a semiconductor.
germaniumเจอร์เมเนียม (Germanium)Element number 32, symbol Ge. A brittle white metal that melts at 937.4 °C. It has semiconducting properties; the compound magnesium germanate is used in fluorescent lamps.
goldทองคำ (Gold)Element number 79, symbol Au. A metal; a very soft yellow solid that melts at 1063 °C. It can be beaten into sheets less than 0.0001 millimetres thick and is used for jewellery and coinage. The purity of gold is now measured in carats, with 24-carat gold being the purest.
hafniumแฮฟเนียม (Hafnium)Element number 72, symbol Hf. A metal; a grey solid that melts at 2150 °C. Used for control rods in water-cooled nuclear reactors.
hassiumฮาสเซียม (Hassium)Element number 108, symbol Hs (not yet added to the Royal Institute Dictionary)
heliumฮีเลียม (Helium)Element number 2, symbol He. An inert gas present at only 1 part in 200,000 in the atmosphere.
holmiumโฮลเมียม (Holmium)Element number 67, symbol Ho. A metal; a lustrous solid that melts at 1461 °C.
hydrogenไฮโดรเจน (Hydrogen)Element number 1, symbol H. A colourless, odourless, tasteless and highly flammable gas, the lightest of all gases. It has many uses, e.g. in the synthesis of ammonia and methyl alcohol and in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils.
indiumอินเดียม (Indium)Element number 49, symbol In. A metal; a soft silvery-white solid that melts at 156.2 °C. It has many uses, e.g. in electronic components, in dental alloys, and for plating silver-coated iron.
iodineไอโอดีน (Iodine)Element number 53, symbol I. A non-metal; a lustrous grey-black solid that melts at 114 °C and sublimes into a violet vapour. An essential element for the thyroid gland; a deficiency causes goitre.
iridiumอิริเดียม (Iridium)Element number 77, symbol Ir. A metal; a very hard silvery-white solid, the heaviest element known, melting at 2454 °C. It is the most corrosion-resistant metal and is used in alloys with other metals.
ironเหล็ก (Iron)Element number 26, symbol Fe. A metal; a lustrous silvery-white solid that melts at 1536 °C. It has many uses, e.g. making cast iron, wrought iron and steel.
kryptonคริปทอน (Krypton)Element number 36, symbol Kr. An inert gas present at only 1 part in 670,000 in the atmosphere.
lanthanumแลนทานัม (Lanthanum)Element number 57, symbol La. A metal; a white solid that melts at 920 °C.
lawrenciumลอว์เรนเซียม (Lawrencium)Element number 103, symbol Lr (Lw is also used). A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
leadตะกั่ว (Lead)Element number 82, symbol Pb. A bluish-white metal; a soft solid that melts at 327.4 °C. Used in alloys with other metals; lead compounds are used in the paint industry. Lead and its compounds are toxic to the body.
lithiumลิเทียม (Lithium)Element number 3, symbol Li. A metal; a silvery solid, the lightest of all solid metals. Melts at 180.5 °C.
lutetiumลูทีเชียม (Lutetium)Element number 71, symbol Lu. A metal; a soft solid that melts at 1652 °C.
magnesiumแมกนีเซียม (Magnesium)Element number 12, symbol Mg. A metal; a silvery solid that melts at 650 °C. When ignited in air it burns with a brilliant white flame. Used in photography, incendiary bombs, lightweight alloys with other metals, etc.
manganeseแมงกานีส (Manganese)Element number 25, symbol Mn. A metal; a hard but brittle silvery solid that melts at 1245 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
meitneriumไมต์เนเรียม (Meitnerium)Element number 109, symbol Mt (not yet added to the Royal Institute Dictionary)
mendeleviumเมนเดลีเวียม (Mendelevium)Element number 101, symbol Md. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
mercuryปรอท (Mercury)Element number 80, symbol Hg. A metal; a silvery liquid that freezes at -38.36 °C and boils at 357 °C. Used to make thermometers, barometers and alloys called amalgam, which are used in dentistry and other scientific instruments. Mercury compounds are toxic, but some are used as medicines.
molybdenumโมลิบดีนัม (Molybdenum)Element number 42, symbol Mo. A metal; a white solid that melts at 2610 °C. Used in alloys with other metals and in making steel.
neodymiumนีโอดิเมียม (Neodymium)Element number 60, symbol Nd. A metal; a pale yellowish solid that melts at 1024 °C.
neonนีออน (Neon)Element number 10, symbol Ne. An inert gas present at only 1 part in 55,000 in the atmosphere.
neptuniumเนปทูเนียม (Neptunium)Element number 93, symbol Np. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature; a metal, a silvery solid.
nickelนิกเกิล (Nickel)Element number 28, symbol Ni. A metal; a silvery solid that melts at 1453 °C. Used in alloys with other metals, for plating other metals, etc.
niobiumไนโอเบียม (Niobium)Element number 41, symbol Nb. A rare metal; a grey solid that melts at 2468 °C. Alloyed with stainless steel to make it resistant to corrosion and high temperatures.
nitrogenไนโตรเจน (Nitrogen)Element number 7, symbol N. A non-metal; a colourless, odourless gas that is chemically unreactive, making up about 80 percent of the atmosphere. It is vital to living things as a key component of proteins and nucleic acids.
nobeliumโนเบเลียม (Nobelium)Element number 102, symbol No. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
osmiumออสเมียม (Osmium)Element number 76, symbol Os. A metal; a very hard white solid that melts at 3000 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
oxygenออกซิเจน (Oxygen)Element number 8, symbol O. A gas making up about 20 percent of air by volume; colourless, odourless, tasteless and non-flammable, but it supports combustion. Essential for respiration and combustion; burned with acetylene for welding or cutting metal, and used in medicine to assist patients' breathing.
palladiumแพลเลเดียม (Palladium)Element number 46, symbol Pd. A metal; a silvery solid similar to platinum that melts at 1552 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
phosphorusฟอสฟอรัส (Phosphorus)Element number 15, symbol P. A non-metal; a solid with several allotropes. The main ones are white phosphorus (sometimes called yellow phosphorus), soft and waxy, melting at 44 °C, easily ignited, glowing on contact with air and highly toxic; and red phosphorus, a reddish-violet powder that does not glow in air, is hard to ignite and is not toxic like white phosphorus.
platinumแพลทินัม (Platinum)Element number 78, symbol Pt. A metal; a lustrous silvery solid that melts at 1769 °C. Used in alloys with other metals, in electrical equipment and scientific instruments, and in high-value jewellery.
plutoniumพลูโทเนียม (Plutonium)Element number 94, symbol Pu. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
poloniumพอโลเนียม (Polonium)Element number 84, symbol Po. A radioactive element; a solid that melts at 254 °C.
potassiumโพแทสเซียม (Potassium)Element number 19, symbol K. A metal; a soft silvery-white solid that melts at 63.7 °C.
praseodymiumเพรซีโอดิเมียม (Praseodymium)Element number 59, symbol Pr. A metal; a pale yellowish solid that melts at 935 °C.
promethiumโพรมีเทียม (Promethium)Element number 61, symbol Pm. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature; a solid that melts at 1027 °C.
protoactinium; protactiniumโพรโทแอกทิเนียม (Protactinium)Element number 91, symbol Pa. A metal; a light grey solid that melts at 1230 °C. A radioactive element, also called โพรแทกทิเนียม.
radiumเรเดียม (Radium)Element number 88, symbol Ra. A naturally occurring radioactive element; a very rare metal that melts at 700 °C. Used in medicine to treat cancer.
radonเรดอน (Radon)Element number 86, symbol Rn. A naturally occurring radioactive gas; an inert gas.
rheniumรีเนียม (Rhenium)Element number 75, symbol Re. A metal; a grey solid that melts at 3180 °C. Used in alloys with other metals, in electrical equipment, and as a component of heat-resistant metals in rockets.
rhodiumโรเดียม (Rhodium)Element number 45, symbol Rh. A metal; a silvery solid that melts at 1966 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
rubidiumรูบิเดียม (Rubidium)Element number 37, symbol Rb. A metal; a soft white solid that is extremely reactive chemically. Melts at 38.9 °C.
rutheniumรูทีเนียม (Ruthenium)Element number 44, symbol Ru. A metal; a brittle silvery solid that melts at 2310 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
rutherfordiumรัทเทอร์ฟอร์เดียม (Rutherfordium)Element number 104, symbol Rf. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature. In the Soviet Union it was called kurchatovium, with the symbol Ku.
samariumซาแมเรียม (Samarium)Element number 62, symbol Sm. A rare metal; a solid that melts at 1072 °C.
scandiumสแกนเดียม (Scandium)Element number 21, symbol Sc. A rare metal; a white solid that melts at 1539 °C.
seaborgiumซีบอร์เกียม (Seaborgium)Element number 106, symbol Sg (not yet added to the Royal Institute Dictionary)
seleniumซีลีเนียม (Selenium)Element number 34, symbol Se. A non-metal with chemical properties similar to sulfur; a solid that melts at 217 °C. Used to make photoelectric cells.
siliconซิลิคอน (Silicon)Element number 14, symbol Si. A non-metal; a solid that melts at 1410 °C. It makes up about 25 percent of the Earth's crust.
silverเงิน (Silver)Element number 47, symbol Ag. A fairly soft white metal that melts at 960.8 °C.
sodiumโซเดียม (Sodium)Element number 11, symbol Na. A soft silvery-white metal that melts at 97.8 °C. Its most common important compound is table salt.
strontiumสตรอนเชียม (Strontium)Element number 38, symbol Sr. A metal; a soft pale yellow solid that is chemically reactive. Melts at 752 °C.
sulphurกำมะถัน (Sulfur)Element number 16, symbol S. A non-metal; a solid with several allotropes. It has many uses, e.g. in the manufacture of sulfuric acid, in the rubber industry, and in making match heads, gunpowder, fireworks and medicines; sulfa drugs and penicillin also contain sulfur.
tantalumแทนทาลัม (Tantalum)Element number 73, symbol Ta. A greyish-white metal; a solid that melts at 2996 °C. Used for light bulb filaments and in alloys with other metals.
technetiumเทคนีเชียม (Technetium)Element number 43, symbol Tc. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
telluriumเทลลูเรียม (Tellurium)Element number 52, symbol Te. A silvery-white solid with chemical properties similar to sulfur; melts at 449.5 °C. It has several allotropes and is used in alloys with other metals and in the coloured glass industry.
terbiumเทอร์เบียม (Terbium)Element number 65, symbol Tb. A metal; a solid that melts at 1356 °C.
thalliumแทลเลียม (Thallium)Element number 81, symbol Tl. A metal; a white solid that melts at 303 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
thoriumทอเรียม (Thorium)Element number 90, symbol Th. A metal; a dark grey solid that melts at 1750 °C. A radioactive element used in alloys with other metals.
thuliumทูเลียม (Thulium)Element number 69, symbol Tm. A metal; a solid that melts at 1545 °C.
tinดีบุก (Tin)Element number 50, symbol Sn. A metal; a soft silvery-white solid that melts at 231.9 °C. It has 3 allotropes: grey tin, white tin and rhombic tin. Used to coat iron against rust and in alloys; thin tin foil is used to wrap things against moisture.
titaniumไทเทเนียม (Titanium)Element number 22, symbol Ti. A metal; a solid that melts at 1668 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
tungstenทังสเตน (Tungsten)Element number 74, symbol W. A metal; a grey solid that melts at 3410 °C. Used for light bulb filaments and in alloys with other metals; also called วุลแฟรม (wolfram).
uraniumยูเรเนียม (Uranium)Element number 92, symbol U. A metal; a hard white solid that melts at 1132 °C. A naturally occurring radioactive element used as nuclear fuel.
vanadiumวาเนเดียม (Vanadium)Element number 23, symbol V. A metal; a white solid that melts at 1900 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
xenonซีนอน (Xenon)Element number 54, symbol Xe. An inert gas present at only 0.006 parts per million in the atmosphere.
ytterbiumอิตเทอร์เบียม (Ytterbium)Element number 70, symbol Yb. A metal; a lustrous solid that melts at 824 °C.
yttriumอิตเทรียม (Yttrium)Element number 39, symbol Y. A metal; a dark grey solid that melts at 1500 °C. Used in alloys with other metals and in nuclear technology.
zincสังกะสี (Zinc)Element number 30, symbol Zn. A metal; a bluish-white solid that melts at 419 °C. It has many uses, e.g. in alloys with other metals and for coating iron against rust.
zirconiumเซอร์โคเนียม (Zirconium)Element number 40, symbol Zr. A rare metal; a solid that melts at 1852 °C.
